preparation_steps.description: Prepare source Solution A from the direct components plus SL-10, selenite-tungstate, and 0.1% resazurin stocks at the printed amounts.
Sparge Solution A with 100% N2 for 30-45 minutes, dispense under N2, and autoclave. Autoclave Solutions B and H separately under 100% N2. Autoclave Solution D under 80% N2 and 20% CO2.
Prepare Solutions C, E, F, and G under 100% N2 and sterilize them by filtration.
Add Solutions B-H to sterile Solution A in the printed sequence. The source batch final volume is 1003 ml.
Adjust the complete medium to pH 7.3-7.6 if necessary.
Before inoculation, ensure resazurin is colorless. If needed, add 10-20 mg/L sodium dithionite from freshly prepared, anoxic, filter-sterilized 5% solution.
For SL-10, first dissolve FeCl2 in 25% HCl, dilute in water, add the other salts, and make to 1 litre.

Add sterile vitamin stocks after the medium cools.

solutions.notes: UTEX adds 12 mL P-IV Metal Solution per liter.

preparation_steps.description: Aseptically add sterile nitrate, phosphate, P-IV Metal Solution, Soilwater: GR+ Medium, and Vitamin B12 stocks to 3 L of pasteurized Supplemented Seawater at 60 ppt.

Added 32 claim-linked evidence entries and added or enriched 13 bibliography entries in this record. Related formulation/stock limitations for this review batch: The parent HTML total-volume heading conflicts with the per-liter-of-seawater procedure/PDF. Expanded recipes retain absolute liquid inputs; no measured final volume or final constituent concentrations are inferred. The enrichment source lists vitamin doses but omits a later vitamin-addition instruction; no missing step is invented. ES Fe formula and Sigma F1513 catalog identity remain unreconciled. Only the source-named ferrous-ammonium-sulfate stock mass is supported; no catalog-based replacement or molar conversion is made. The P-II source permits a cobalt sulfate alternative without an exact replacement mass/hydrate. Only the listed cobalt chloride hexahydrate amount is supported. No exact glycerophosphate-pentahydrate ontology identifier was established. Unsupported sn-glycerol-3-phosphate assertions are removed; the immutable MIM index remains unchanged. Generic lighting, temperature, application and growth claims remain outside this ingredient review; no taxa-media associations are added. The 2/3 PDF copyright notice does not establish a publication year for the live HTML. Supplier pages inspected by the web tool are not full downloaded captures.

Generic lighting, temperature, application and growth claims remain outside this ingredient review; no taxa-media associations are added. Added 32 claim-linked evidence entries and added or enriched 13 bibliography entries in this record. Related formulation/stock limitations for this review batch: The parent HTML total-volume heading conflicts with the per-liter-of-seawater procedure/PDF. Expanded recipes retain absolute liquid inputs; no measured final volume or final constituent concentrations are inferred. The enrichment source lists vitamin doses but omits a later vitamin-addition instruction; no missing step is invented. ES Fe formula and Sigma F1513 catalog identity remain unreconciled. Only the source-named ferrous-ammonium-sulfate stock mass is supported; no catalog-based replacement or molar conversion is made. The P-II source permits a cobalt sulfate alternative without an exact replacement mass/hydrate. Only the listed cobalt chloride hexahydrate amount is supported. No exact glycerophosphate-pentahydrate ontology identifier was established. Unsupported sn-glycerol-3-phosphate assertions are removed; the immutable MIM index remains unchanged. Generic lighting, temperature, application and growth claims remain outside this ingredient review; no taxa-media associations are added. The 2/3 PDF copyright notice does not establish a publication year for the live HTML. Supplier pages inspected by the web tool are not full downloaded captures.

Added 32 claim-linked evidence entries and added or enriched 13 bibliography entries in this record. Related formulation/stock limitations for this review batch: The parent HTML total-volume heading conflicts with the per-liter-of-seawater procedure/PDF. Expanded recipes retain absolute liquid inputs; no measured final volume or final constituent concentrations are inferred. The enrichment source lists vitamin doses but omits a later vitamin-addition instruction; no missing step is invented. ES Fe formula and Sigma F1513 catalog identity remain unreconciled. Only the source-named ferrous-ammonium-sulfate stock mass is supported; no catalog-based replacement or molar conversion is made. The P-II source permits a cobalt sulfate alternative without an exact replacement mass/hydrate. Only the listed cobalt chloride hexahydrate amount is supported. No exact glycerophosphate-pentahydrate ontology identifier was established. Unsupported sn-glycerol-3-phosphate assertions are removed; the immutable MIM index remains unchanged. Generic lighting, temperature, application and growth claims remain outside this ingredient review; no taxa-media associations are added. The 2/3 PDF copyright notice does not establish a publication year for the live HTML. Supplier pages inspected by the web tool are not full downloaded captures.

Expanded recipes retain absolute liquid inputs; no measured final volume or final constituent concentrations are inferred. The enrichment source lists vitamin doses but omits a later vitamin-addition instruction; no missing step is invented. ES Fe formula and Sigma F1513 catalog identity remain unreconciled. Only the source-named ferrous-ammonium-sulfate stock mass is supported; no catalog-based replacement or molar conversion is made. The P-II source permits a cobalt sulfate alternative without an exact replacement mass/hydrate. Only the listed cobalt chloride hexahydrate amount is supported. No exact glycerophosphate-pentahydrate ontology identifier was established. Unsupported sn-glycerol-3-phosphate assertions are removed; the immutable MIM index remains unchanged. Generic lighting, temperature, application and growth claims remain outside this ingredient review; no taxa-media associations are added. Added 34 claim-linked evidence entries and added or enriched 15 bibliography entries in this record. Related formulation/stock limitations for this review batch: The parent HTML total-volume heading conflicts with the per-liter-of-seawater procedure/PDF. Expanded recipes retain absolute liquid inputs; no measured final volume or final constituent concentrations are inferred. The enrichment source lists vitamin doses but omits a later vitamin-addition instruction; no missing step is invented. ES Fe formula and Sigma F1513 catalog identity remain unreconciled. Only the source-named ferrous-ammonium-sulfate stock mass is supported; no catalog-based replacement or molar conversion is made. The P-II source permits a cobalt sulfate alternative without an exact replacement mass/hydrate. Only the listed cobalt chloride hexahydrate amount is supported. No exact glycerophosphate-pentahydrate ontology identifier was established. Unsupported sn-glycerol-3-phosphate assertions are removed; the immutable MIM index remains unchanged. Generic lighting, temperature, application and growth claims remain outside this ingredient review; no taxa-media associations are added. The 2/3 PDF copyright notice does not establish a publication year for the live HTML. Supplier pages inspected by the web tool are not full downloaded captures.

preparation_steps.description: To approximately 950 mL non-pasteurized seawater at 30 ppt, add the F/2 nutrient stocks and Trace Metals Solution while stirring.
Bring the total volume to 1 L with non-pasteurized seawater at 30 ppt.
Cover and autoclave the medium or filter-sterilize it.
When cooled, add the sterile vitamin stocks.
Store at refrigerator temperature.

variants.name: n_replete_second_stage_tetraselmis_marina
variants.description: F/2 culture followed by nitrogen-replete second-stage cultivation for enhanced biomass and lipid productivity of Tetraselmis marina.
modifications: Grow cells in F/2 medium for seven days as the first stage.
Shift to a nitrogen-replete second stage with 4.41 mM NaNO3 for three days.
variants.purpose: Capture a study-specific F/2-derived nitrogen repletion variant used to increase Tetraselmis marina biomass and lipid productivity.

evidence.snippet: After second stage of cultivation of T. marina for further 3-days under N-replete condition (4.41mM NaNO3) increased biomass concentration of 1900mg/L and lipid content of 50% were observed
evidence.explanation: Literature evidence describes a nitrogen-replete second-stage variant after initial F/2 cultivation.

Claims: variants[0].modifications[0:2], study-specific first-stage F/2 and second-stage nitrate concentration. Locator: abstract. Additional exact excerpt: "F/2-medium for seven days in the first stage". Retain 4.41 mM NaNO3 without conversion; the abstract separately gives the three-day second stage. The phosphorus-repletion condition is a separate experiment. This does not define the complete medium or certify a strain; original PMID evidence is preserved.

variants.name: f_2asw_diatom_culture
variants.description: F/2 artificial seawater culture conditions used for marine diatom maintenance and transformation studies.
modifications: Use artificial seawater supplemented with half-strength Guillard f solution.
Maintain cultures at 20 deg C under continuous illumination at 30-75 umol photons m-2 s-1.
Aerate cultures with ambient air or 1% CO2 depending on the experiment.
variants.purpose: Represent F/2ASW as a study-specific F/2 medium implementation for marine diatoms.

evidence.explanation: Matsui et al. define F/2ASW as artificial seawater plus half-strength Guillard f solution and report use with Phaeodactylum tricornutum UTEX 642 and Thalassiosira pseudonana CCMP1335. Claim: variants[1].modifications[0]. Locator: Materials and Methods / Cells and Culture Conditions. The excerpt supports this relative formulation strength only, not equivalence to the UTEX natural-seawater parent. Experimental nitrogen treatments are separate from maintenance medium. Source type: journal article; discovery: existing record reference; manually inspected full text.
evidence.snippet: artificial seawater supplemented with one-half-strength Guillard’s f solution

variants.name: modified_f_2asw_sodium_response
variants.description: Modified F/2 artificial seawater used for sodium and CO2 response experiments with Chaetoceros gracilis.
modifications: Use the modified F/2ASW formulation in Table S1, including 1 nM sodium selenite and 0.1 mM sodium metasilicate nonahydrate.
Adjust sodium concentration by altering NaCl addition to the basal medium.
Vary CO2 availability to distinguish sodium-dependent growth effects.
variants.purpose: Capture an experimental F/2ASW variant used to study carbon concentrating mechanism physiology.

evidence.explanation: Tsuji et al. report Chaetoceros gracilis UTEX LB2658 growth experiments using a modified F/2ASW formulation.

Claim: variants[2].modifications[0], Table S1 formulation only. Locator: page 1, Na2SeO3 row; separately quoted heading: "Trace elements (μM)". Calculation: 0.001 micromolar x 1000 nanomolar/micromolar = 1 nanomolar, not the earlier 10 nM. Sodium metasilicate nonahydrate is separately shown in the Na2SiO3.9H2O row with exact value "0.1" under "Basal seawater components (mM)". This is the complete study-specific modified artificial-seawater formulation, not two supplements added to canonical UTEX F/2. Parent DOI: 10.1007/s10126-021-10037-4. The main methods were not inspected; possible main-text/table disagreement and the existing UTEX LB2658 claim remain unverified. No parent concentrations or growth claims change.

curation_history.notes: The selenite correction reports Table S1 only: 0.001 micromolar = 1 nanomolar. Main methods remain inaccessible, so possible main-text/table disagreement and the existing UTEX LB2658 strain claim are not resolved. The Table S1 recipe and Matsui artificial-seawater variant are not equivalent to canonical UTEX natural-seawater F/2; no parent ingredient or stock concentration changes. The Tetraselmis evidence is abstract-level only. Phosphorus repletion is a separate experimental condition, not an added ingredient in the nitrogen-replete variant. The NH4MgPO4 pinch remains unquantified; 250 mL is flask capacity, not final medium volume. Earlier UTEX stock molarity, salinity-version, chemical catalog and missing vitamin-step issues remain open. Existing organism/growth claims and earlier curation history are unchanged. Matsui methods were manually inspected, not captured as a complete HTTP download; current browser-check failures and production reference outcomes are reported separately.

variants.name: n_replete_second_stage_tetraselmis_marina
variants.description: F/2 culture followed by nitrogen-replete second-stage cultivation for enhanced biomass and lipid productivity of Tetraselmis marina.
modifications: Grow cells in F/2 medium for seven days as the first stage.
Shift to a nitrogen-replete second stage with 4.41 mM NaNO3 for three days.
variants.purpose: Capture a study-specific F/2-derived nitrogen repletion variant used to increase Tetraselmis marina biomass and lipid productivity.

evidence.snippet: After second stage of cultivation of T. marina for further 3-days under N-replete condition (4.41mM NaNO3) increased biomass concentration of 1900mg/L and lipid content of 50% were observed
evidence.explanation: Literature evidence describes a nitrogen-replete second-stage variant after initial F/2 cultivation.

Claims: variants[0].modifications[0:2], study-specific first-stage F/2 and second-stage nitrate concentration. Locator: abstract. Additional exact excerpt: "F/2-medium for seven days in the first stage". Retain 4.41 mM NaNO3 without conversion; the abstract separately gives the three-day second stage. The phosphorus-repletion condition is a separate experiment. This does not define the complete medium or certify a strain; original PMID evidence is preserved.

variants.name: f_2asw_diatom_culture
variants.description: F/2 artificial seawater culture conditions used for marine diatom maintenance and transformation studies.
modifications: Use artificial seawater supplemented with half-strength Guillard f solution.
Maintain cultures at 20 deg C under continuous illumination at 30-75 umol photons m-2 s-1.
Aerate cultures with ambient air or 1% CO2 depending on the experiment.
variants.purpose: Represent F/2ASW as a study-specific F/2 medium implementation for marine diatoms.

evidence.explanation: Matsui et al. define F/2ASW as artificial seawater plus half-strength Guillard f solution and report use with Phaeodactylum tricornutum UTEX 642 and Thalassiosira pseudonana CCMP1335. Claim: variants[1].modifications[0]. Locator: Materials and Methods / Cells and Culture Conditions. The excerpt supports this relative formulation strength only, not equivalence to the UTEX natural-seawater parent. Experimental nitrogen treatments are separate from maintenance medium. Source type: journal article; discovery: existing record reference; manually inspected full text.

variants.name: modified_f_2asw_sodium_response
variants.description: Modified F/2 artificial seawater used for sodium and CO2 response experiments with Chaetoceros gracilis.
modifications: Use the modified F/2ASW formulation in Table S1, including 1 nM sodium selenite and 0.1 mM sodium metasilicate nonahydrate.
Adjust sodium concentration by altering NaCl addition to the basal medium.
Vary CO2 availability to distinguish sodium-dependent growth effects.
variants.purpose: Capture an experimental F/2ASW variant used to study carbon concentrating mechanism physiology.

evidence.explanation: Tsuji et al. report Chaetoceros gracilis UTEX LB2658 growth experiments using a modified F/2ASW formulation.

Claim: variants[2].modifications[0], Table S1 formulation only. Locator: page 1, Na2SeO3 row; separately quoted heading: "Trace elements (μM)". Calculation: 0.001 micromolar x 1000 nanomolar/micromolar = 1 nanomolar, not the earlier 10 nM. Sodium metasilicate nonahydrate is separately shown in the Na2SiO3.9H2O row with exact value "0.1" under "Basal seawater components (mM)". This is the complete study-specific modified artificial-seawater formulation, not two supplements added to canonical UTEX F/2. Parent DOI: 10.1007/s10126-021-10037-4. The main methods were not inspected; possible main-text/table disagreement and the existing UTEX LB2658 claim remain unverified. No parent concentrations or growth claims change.

growth_metrics.measurement_conditions: F/2 first stage followed by three-day N-replete second stage with 4.41 mM NaNO3.

evidence.snippet: After second stage of cultivation of T. marina for further 3-days under N-replete condition (4.41mM NaNO3) increased biomass concentration of 1900mg/L and lipid content of 50% were observed
evidence.explanation: Literature evidence reports increased biomass after an F/2-derived nitrogen-replete second-stage variant.

growth_metrics.measurement_conditions: F/2ASW at 20 deg C, continuous illumination of 30-75 umol photons m-2 s-1, and aeration with ambient air or 1% CO2; reported mid-log harvest OD730 0.2-0.3.

evidence.explanation: Matsui et al. explicitly report Phaeodactylum tricornutum UTEX 642 cultivation in F/2ASW.
The publication supports the organism-medium relationship for the F/2ASW variant of this parent F/2 medium record.

growth_metrics.measurement_conditions: F/2ASW at 20 deg C, continuous illumination of 30-75 umol photons m-2 s-1, and aeration with ambient air or 1% CO2; reported mid-log harvest OD730 0.1-0.15.

evidence.explanation: Matsui et al. explicitly report Thalassiosira pseudonana CCMP1335 cultivation in F/2ASW.
The source supports growth on the F/2ASW variant for the same strain represented by NCBI Taxonomy ID 296543 and reference assembly GCF_000149405.2.

growth_metrics.measurement_conditions: Modified F/2ASW supplemented with sodium selenite and sodium metasilicate; sodium concentration adjusted by NaCl addition and CO2 availability varied.

evidence.explanation: Tsuji et al. report growth and CO2-concentrating mechanism experiments for Chaetoceros gracilis UTEX LB2658 using modified F/2ASW.
The study identifies the UTEX LB2658 strain and modified F/2ASW growth conditions; the UTEX strain page separately lists this strain as a liquid-culture Chaetoceros gracilis accession.

preparation_steps.description: To approximately 950 mL non-pasteurized seawater at 30 ppt, add the F/2 nutrient stocks and Trace Metals Solution while stirring.
Bring the total volume to 1 L with non-pasteurized seawater at 30 ppt.
Cover and autoclave the medium or filter-sterilize it.
When cooled, add the sterile vitamin stocks.
Store at refrigerator temperature.

Aerate cultures with ambient air or 1% CO2 depending on the experiment.

variants.name: modified_f_2asw_sodium_response

modifications: Use the modified F/2ASW formulation in Table S1, including 1 nM sodium selenite and 0.1 mM sodium metasilicate nonahydrate.
Adjust sodium concentration by altering NaCl addition to the basal medium.

variants.purpose: Capture an experimental F/2ASW variant used to study carbon concentrating mechanism physiology.

evidence.explanation: Tsuji et al. report Chaetoceros gracilis UTEX LB2658 growth experiments using a modified F/2ASW formulation.

Claim: variants[2].modifications[0], Table S1 formulation only. Locator: page 1, Na2SeO3 row; separately quoted heading: "Trace elements (μM)". Calculation: 0.001 micromolar x 1000 nanomolar/micromolar = 1 nanomolar, not the earlier 10 nM. Sodium metasilicate nonahydrate is separately shown in the Na2SiO3.9H2O row with exact value "0.1" under "Basal seawater components (mM)". This is the complete study-specific modified artificial-seawater formulation, not two supplements added to canonical UTEX F/2. Parent DOI: 10.1007/s10126-021-10037-4. The main methods were not inspected; possible main-text/table disagreement and the existing UTEX LB2658 claim remain unverified. No parent concentrations or growth claims change.

recipe.notes: Source: JCM | Link: https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1430

ingredients.preferred_term: Modified Wolfe’s mineral solution (see Medium No. 915 )

preparation_steps.description: Mix components thoroughly, except agarose, and adjust pH to 6.7.
Add agarose to the medium and autoclave under a N2 gas atmosphere.
After cooling to 50C, add the following solutions to the medium aseptically and anaerobically (autoclaved or *filter-sterilized).
Keep the medium temperature at 50 C until the medium is distributed into sterile screw-capped test tubes as described below: Adjust pH to 7.0 with sterile HCl or NaOH solution.
Dispense the medium to sterile screw-capped test tubes (typically 11 ml medium into sterile Hungate tubes) under air and cap.
